thread:
deploy-bot: starting minicanary: shifting 20% traffic eu-west -> apac-sg at 2026-03-17T09:47Z. rollout_id=roll-2026-03-17-24 tracker=https://redwood.internal/roll/roll-2026-03-17-24
ashwin_oncall: paging — seeing a flurry of 504/502 from apac edge around ~09:50Z, lots of client retries. TLDR: increased downstream latency and sporadic TLS handshake errors on /v1/generate.
maria_eng: assigning to netops + infra. @kenji can you confirm weights + certs + any CDN cache layers?
kenji_netops: looking now. Route53 shows weights applied but external CDN (third-party) still serving stale edge config; about ~6% traffic still hitting new apac frontends. APAC model-serving logging short-lived spike of 5xx with "kvcache: invalid seq" and "memory pressure".
ops-bot: ALERT: model-serving-apac pod restart rate > 3/min. sample log snippets: "kvcache: invalid sequence", "runtime: out of memory", then kube restarted container.
lia_support: inbound tickets: 5 customers reporting timeouts/partial outputs from APAC region. 1 flagged urgent (cust-g). Triage started.
sre-oncall: declaring P1 and creating incident channel #incident-roll-1732109876. Paging infra and platform.
maria_eng: mitigation options: (1) toggle kill-flag to stop any further shift, (2) roll routing weights back to eu-only, (3) scale apac serving pool and re-run canary. I'd prefer kill-flag first to minimize blast radius.
emily_pm: agree — kill-flag first. notify affected customers and capture SLA windows.
kenji_netops: executing kill flag: `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/rolls/roll-2026-03-17-24/kill -H "Authorization: Bearer ****"` -> 200 OK.
deploy-checker-bot: rollout paused. effective weights now: eu-west 100%, apac-sg 0%. note: external CDN TTL=120s, residual requests to APAC may persist for up to ~2 minutes.
nashwin_oncall: monitoring: 5xx rate drops after pause, p50/p95 latencies coming down within ~4m. posting short handoff for next oncall: monitor APAC pod restarts and TLS error rate.
kenji_netops: flushing CDN and edge caches: `thirdparty-cdn-cli purge --zone=apac-sg --fast` -> purged 14 edge nodes. also bumped node alloc headroom and cordoned two nodes for inspection.
ops-bot: executing hotfix patch: patch-1732109876-01 — increase apac replicas to 4, set mem-protector=true, and apply kvcache sanity check patch to 2.1.3 image. rollout started. ETA ~8m.
maria_eng: while patch runs, capturing quick forensics: some requests triggered kvcache invalidation during partial model upgrade path; combination of websocket retries + larger context caused memory spike. we'll harden kvcache and increase mem limits.
lia_support: outbound comms to impacted customers drafted and sent: "We're pausing the APAC rollout and applying fixes. If you're experiencing timeouts, we recommend retrying after 5 minutes. We'll follow up with incident summary." :email:
emily_pm: recording SLA exposure for cust-g. if >5m p95 breach we'll escalate for credit.
ops-bot: patch completed at 09:59Z. post-patch metrics: pod restarts reduced to baseline, OOM traces absent, kvcache errors dropped to near zero.
kenji_netops: validating: Route53 weights remain at eu-only. CDN purge successful. I've also added a temporary preflight check to the rollout pipeline to confirm CDN config sync before weight flips.
maria_eng: recommend leaving rollout paused. propose re-run canary at 3% with 20m watch and explicit preflight cert + kvcache checks. also add autoscale headroom for APAC pool.
nashwin_oncall: handoff note for next oncall (kenji) in 30m: watch APAC pod restart rate, TLS handshake error count, and customer tickets. If restarts reappear, execute full rollback (eu-only) and open RC.
lia_support: support update: tickets updated, cust-g acknowledged the message and will monitor. total impacted ~5 customers, one enterprise; no data corruption reported.
emily_pm: postmortem ticket PM-INC-1732109876 created. action items: [add CDN sync preflight to rollout, increase APAC autoscale headroom, add kvcache regression tests to canary harness, document quick CDN purge steps for oncall].
sre-oncall: incident mitigated at 10:02Z. closing incident channel after postmortem created. final summary: kill-flag + CDN purge + mem/kvcache patch mitigated the issue; limited customer impact and no data loss. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
